mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC AJ126 engine typically costs between £6,000 and £9,500 for supply only, with supply and fit packages ranging from £8,000 to £11,500 depending on the specialist. - Supply-only rebuilt: £6,000-£9,500 [EM-QUOTE] - Supply & fit: £8,000-£11,500 [ESTIMATED] - Always ensure the quote includes a minimum 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of coolant or water pump failure in a Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AJ126 V6 is prone to plastic coolant crossover pipe degradation and water pump failure. Early warning signs include unexplained coolant loss, sweet smells from the engine bay, overheating warnings, or white smoke from the exhaust. - Monitor the coolant reservoir for unexplained drops in level. - Check for external leaks around the water pump and crossover pipes. - Address overheating warnings immediately to prevent catastrophic internal damage.

mainEntity.name: Is the 3.0 SC (Si6) more reliable than the 5.0 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the 3.0 SC AJ126 is generally considered more reliable than the 5.0L AJ133 V8. While both share some supercharger and cooling system characteristics, the AJ126 avoids the severe timing chain tensioner and oil consumption issues that plague the high-output 5.0L V8 at higher mileages. - The AJ126 has fewer catastrophic bottom-end failure reports. - Cooling system maintenance is critical for both engines. - Rebuilt AJ126 units include upgraded preventative components.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, investing in a rebuilt engine is financially sound. With Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC values currently ranging from £12,000 to over £25,000 depending on condition, a £6,000-£9,500 replacement is well within the vehicle's value band and preserves this premium asset. - Premium Range Rover Sport values easily absorb rebuild costs. - A rebuilt engine resets the mechanical lifespan with upgraded components. - Upgraded cooling and supercharger parts prevent repeat failures.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit service for a Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC typically takes 3 to 5 days at a specialist workshop. The complex supercharger system and tight engine bay require meticulous removal and calibration. - Removal and installation: 2-3 days. - Fluid top-up, system bleeding, and ECU calibration: 1-2 days. - Always confirm turnaround times with your chosen specialist.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC (Si6) delivers supercharged V6 performance, but its cooling system and supercharger drivetrain introduce specific wear points. The AJ126 engine dominates replacement demand for mid-2010s petrol Sports, primarily due to coolant crossover leaks and timing chain tensioner wear. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks & Water Pump Failure
problems.h4: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks & Water Pump Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC AJ126 Overheats
problems.rootCause: The plastic coolant crossover pipes and water pump impellers degrade under high underbonnet temperatures, leading to sudden coolant loss and potential overheating if not addressed promptly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace degraded plastic crossover pipes with upgraded aluminium alternatives, fit new water pump, and pressure test the system.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable for isolated leaks if the engine block and internals are otherwise healthy and overheating was caught early.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt AJ126 with upgraded cooling components and revised crossover pipes, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if overheating has already caused secondary internal damage or warped cylinder heads.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC (2015-2017) currently holds a value of £12,000-£25,000 in the UK [THIRD-PARTY]. A £6,000-£9,500 rebuilt engine replacement sits comfortably within the vehicle's value band. Flag: Safe.
problems.recommendation: For isolated coolant leaks, specialist pipe and water pump replacement with upgraded components is highly cost-effective. However, if the engine has overheated, a rebuilt unit provides a comprehensive, warrantied reset.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt AJ126 Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC engine prices

problems.group: Timing Chain Tensioner & Supercharger Coupler Wear
problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Supercharger Coupler Wear - Why the Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC AJ126 Rattles
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioners can wear over time, leading to a distinct cold-start rattle, while the supercharger coupler can degrade, causing a whining noise from the top of the engine and reduced boost efficiency.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace worn timing chain tensioners and inspect/replace the supercharger coupler and nose seal.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for isolated wear if the chain has not stretched excessively or jumped teeth.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt AJ126 with an upgraded timing chain kit and revised supercharger components, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Best if the timing chain has rattled extensively, skipped teeth, or if the engine has high mileage alongside multiple wear indicators.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As noted, Range Rover Sport 3.0 SC values (£12,000-£25,000) easily absorb the cost of a full rebuild, making it a sound investment over repeated minor repairs.
problems.recommendation: If the cold-start rattle is minor and boost pressure is unaffected, specialist tensioner and coupler replacement is cost-effective. For significant noise, performance loss, or high mileage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components provides a comprehensive, warrantied reset.
